args.code:
# Based on the disassembly:
# The loop at 0x40114c does:
# - edx starts at 0xffffffad (-83 or 173 unsigned as byte)
# - For each character at position rax (0..24):
#   - ecx = input[rax]
#   - esi = ecx ^ edx
#   - compare sil (low byte of esi) with target_ct[rax]
#   - if match: edx += ecx, rax++
#   - if all 25 match: success
#
# So: target_ct[i] = input[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)
# Therefore: input[i] = target_ct[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)
# After computing input[i], update edx: edx = (edx + input[i]) & 0xffffffff

target_ct = bytes([
    0xeb, 0xbf, 0x7e, 0xc7, 0xbc, 0x25, 0xdb, 0x7a,
    0x12, 0x83, 0x27, 0xa2, 0x73, 0xe9, 0x8c, 0x3d,
    0xa0, 0x4e, 0xfa, 0x5d, 0x50, 0xab, 0xfe, 0x32,
    0x4f
])

# Initial edx = 0xffffffad
edx = 0xffffffad

result = []
for i in range(25):
    edx_byte = edx & 0xff
    char = target_ct[i] ^ edx_byte
    result.append(char)
    edx = (edx + char) & 0xffffffff

answer = bytes(result)
print("Decrypted input:", answer)
print("As string:", answer.decode('latin-1'))
